**The launcher owns the process tree and the clock.** Every entry carries an explicit `timeout` T and a `--deadline` D below it: `D = floor(min(0.95·T, T − 1))`. The harness kills a hook at T without waiting for a verdict, and on Windows that kill leaves the handler's children running. D fires first. Past D the launcher ends the handler's whole process tree and answers itself: a plugin handler gets one stderr line (`verdict unknown`) and exit 0, never a block; a repository handler fails closed as before, with each entry capped to the budget left. On Windows each handler runs in its own Job Object (kill-on-close, no breakaway) nested in a job for the launcher, so killing the launcher also ends the tree; on POSIX each handler is a session leader and the launcher signals its group. `worktree-remove.sh` is the one exception on Windows: it starts a deliberately detached waiter, so it runs with no job and a deadline walks its parent chain. Stop does not wait on a survivor: a killed scan is an unknown verdict. `hooks/native-contract-gate.sh` check M refuses an entry without `timeout` or `--deadline`, or with D at or above the bound; an entry outside the launcher needs a `hook-deadline` line in `hooks/native-contract-allow.txt` naming its own deadline. || deadline rule for every hook entry

claims.text: the hit set holds every reference to create-worktree, remove-worktree, h2_move, worktree-provision over the name forms this pass searched

Starting claim checked: error_exit prints ERROR=<reason> on STDERR and exits 1, and the ERR trap under set -eE routes every other failing simple command of the main shell to it; WORKTREE_PATH=<path> is the script's only STDOUT write. The header's 'always the LAST line' names no stream: ERROR= is the last stderr line, WORKTREE_PATH= the last stdout line.

Every caller reads the contract by stream: worktree-create.sh takes WORKTREE_PATH= from stdout and prints only the bare path; afk-move.py takes WORKTREE_PATH= from stdout and ERROR= from stderr; afk-launch.py takes WORKTREE_PATH= from stdout and on failure raises with the whole stderr.

Five failure points are soft and the script still exits 0 with WORKTREE_PATH=: owner record write (:443-445), copied-file manifest (:483-485), provisioning (:495-496), IDE launch (:502), WorktreeCreated scripts (:512-513).

Failures before the first write leave nothing: bad or combined arguments (:126, :158-164), name rule (:160), branch pattern (:166-169, :233-234), no repository (:200-201), folder outside the repository (:227), destination exists (:255). Each is ERROR= on stderr, exit 1. Pinned for name, pattern and no-repository cases.

Name mode only: the lock is <common>/afk-worktrees/.lock with holder pid:ctime, taken at :386 after mkdir -p <common>/afk-worktrees (:363). The EXIT trap (:382) removes it on every later exit, error_exit included, while this process holds it (:351-357); it is released early at :446. Lock-wait timeout after 600 tries is ERROR= exit 1 with nothing else changed (:377). A killed holder's lock stays until the next creator finds the holder dead (:368-370) or, with no holder file, after 2 minutes (:372-374).

Between the lock and git worktree add: a taken name (folder or owner record exists, :397) or an existing branch (:398) is ERROR= exit 1; left behind is the <common>/afk-worktrees folder, lock removed by the EXIT trap. `git worktree prune` (:402) and `mkdir -p` of the parent (:405) run before the add, so a failed add leaves the parent folder (<repo>/.claude/worktrees in name mode) and, in name mode, no info/exclude line yet (:437 runs after the add).

Inference: if a failed add leaves branch worktree-<name> (or the template's branch), a retry with the same name fails at :398 'branch already exists'; the H-2 retry reuses the recorded name, so it would fail that way every 180 s.

After git worktree add in name mode, a failing mkdir/printf of info/exclude (:436-441) trips the ERR trap: exit 1 with the worktree registered, folder and branch present, no owner record, lock released. A failed owner-record write is soft (:445): exit 0, no record, warning 'will not be pruned automatically'.

A copy-step failure (mkdir, perl or cp inside copy_file_with_substitution :311-320, or .idea/.name :461) trips the ERR trap: ERROR=unexpected failure near line N, exit 1. Left: registered worktree, branch, owner record and exclude lines (name mode), the files copied so far, no afk-copied.json (written only at :482-486), no provisioning, no WorktreeCreated run. Pinned by create-worktree-smoke.sh:170-185, which removes the left worktree itself.

create-worktree treats any non-zero worktree-provision exit as a warning and goes on to exit 0 (:495-496). worktree-provision exits 2 from die() (bad argument, missing worktree, unresolved marker path), 0 when no build gate is selected, 2 at once when an adapter exits 2 (later kinds never run), and 4 when any adapter exited 4 or another code (later kinds still run); exit 3 is a skip.

An adapter exit 4 still leaves a provision marker that says provisioned: both adapters keep STATUS=provisioned on exit 4 and worktree-provision writes status and fingerprint (:158-163), so a later run without --force reports 'already provisioned — unchanged' (:121-133) and never retries the failed install or seed. Unguarded: worktree-provision-smoke.sh has no exit-4 case.

Document finding: maven CONTRACT.md:77-78 gives exit 2 for 'an invalid payload' only, but worktree-provision.sh:169 and :172 also exit 2 through fail() when .mvn cannot be made or maven.config cannot be written; worktree-provision then prints 'refused to provision (invalid configuration or unsafe input)' and stops before the remaining kinds (:149-151). The adapter CLI preambles also exit 2 when git rev-parse fails.

State a provisioning failure leaves: maven adds .mvn/maven.config and .m2/ to COMMON info/exclude (:155-160), appends maven.config and records it in afk-copied.json (worktree_owner.py:334-354), and a failed seed leaves a partial .m2/repository (:196-223); npm leaves whatever the install wrote (:127-136). A kind that exits 2 gets no marker (worktree-provision exits before :158).

IDE open runs in branch mode only (name mode sets OPEN_FLAG=false, :161), in the background with `|| true`, so it never changes the exit code. Inference: its stdout is not redirected (:502), so IDE output could follow the WORKTREE_PATH= line on stdout.

WorktreeCreated scripts run through run-hook.py --soft with output on stderr and `|| true`; a non-zero script is reported 'exited N; the worktree is kept' and the creation exits 0. Pinned by test_create_worktree_name.py:259 and test_protected_branch_acceptance.py:923.

Hook path: worktree-create.sh exits with create-worktree's code, or 1 when it exited 0 without WORKTREE_PATH=, printing nothing on stdout; run-hook.py writes '[afk] worktree-create.sh (WorktreeCreate) failed: exit N' to stderr and, for claude (hook_failure_notice stderr), passes the code through. Pinned by test_create_worktree_name.py:314 and test_hook_failures.py:443.

Deadline: the WorktreeCreate command runs under run-hook.py --deadline 570 (harness timeout 600). Past it the handler tree is killed (Windows TerminateJobObject; POSIX SIGTERM then SIGKILL after 1 s) and run-hook.py drops stdout and exits 0: the harness gets exit 0 with no path. Left behind is whatever the killed step had reached: during lock wait or git add, the lock folder (broken later as a dead holder); during provisioning (after :446), the worktree, owner record and copied manifest with provisioning partial and no marker for the killed kind.

H-2 path: h2_move.plan writes <common>/afk-session/<key>.move ({name, path, pane, marker}) by exclusive create, then spawns afk-move.py fully detached. afk-move.py truncates <common>/afk-worktrees/<name>.log, runs create-worktree, writes `created` or `error` (last ERROR= line, else last 300 chars of stderr) into the marker, and exits 1 on failure.

H-2 retry: on the next refusal for the same key, a marker whose path exists and whose owner record is all dead is deleted and a new name chosen (:88-90); a path that exists, or a marker younger than RETRY_AFTER=180 s, returns the recorded body, so the guard shows the recorded error (protected_branch_guard.py:414-417); otherwise the marker is touched and afk-move.py runs again with the SAME name (:91-99); the old error stays until record() pops it (afk-move.py:126). Pinned: test_h2_move.py:283 (error recorded, second refusal says why); the 180 s retry is unguarded.

Inference: after a failure that left the folder (copy step, exclude write, deadline), the marker's path exists, so no retry runs and every refusal repeats the recorded error while the owner lives. After an afk-move.py crash or its 900 s timeout (not caught in create(), re-raised at :246-250) the marker has no outcome, so the guard keeps saying 'a linked worktree is being created' for an existing half-made folder, or retries after 180 s when no folder exists.
afk-launch.py: any create failure prints 'no worktree was made (<stderr>)' and returns 1 without starting the harness; `made` stays None, so its removal never runs.
Inference: when afk-launch.py's creation fails after git worktree add, its 'no worktree was made' message is false and the half-made worktree is left for the remover (partition B).

Branch mode (--branch/--dir) has no lock, no owner record and no exclude lines (all under `[[ -n "$NAME" ]]`, :385-399, :433-447); the copied manifest, provisioning, IDE open and WorktreeCreated run as in name mode.

Cleaners inside partition A: the EXIT trap and the next creator's dead-holder break clear the lock; `git worktree prune` at every creation (:402) drops admin entries of folders already gone (git behaviour, frontier); h2_move deletes a marker only when its folder exists and its owner is dead (:88-89). Every other leftover — registered worktree, branch, owner record, copied files, .log, .move — is the remover's (partition B): remove-worktree.py drop_record deletes <name>.json and <name>.log (:277-281), drop_markers deletes .move markers naming a removed path (:258-264), worktree-prune.sh calls --prune only when <common>/afk-worktrees exists (:12-14).

Edge for partition B: a half-made worktree from a failure between :428 and :443, from a failed record write, or from branch mode has NO owner record; one from a later failure has an owner record and no afk-copied.json. A .move marker whose path never existed is touched by no cleaner found: `git grep -n -I -E -e '\.move' -e afk-session -- hooks scripts adapters skills` (exit 0) shows .move handling only at h2_move.py:75,89 and remove-worktree.py:253-264.

claims.text: Dynamic loads on the path fail soft except one: h2_move's by-path loads of worktree_owner.py give {} or False on any exception; afk-launch's loads sit inside its try (exit 1); run-hook.py's owner load gives {}; create-worktree sources provider.sh and config.sh under set -eE, and afk_config_load never fails (a failed export sets AFK_CFG_LOAD_FAILED, which no create-path file reads). The exception: afk-move.py's load of run-hook.py is not caught, so the helper dies with no marker outcome.

Entry points into create-worktree in partition A's files: the harness WorktreeCreate hook (hooks.json:80-85 → worktree-create.sh:25), the H-2 helper (afk-move.py:109), the launcher (afk-launch.py:57), and a direct run the move hint asks for (providers/codex.json:21). The wire pass (WorktreeCreate, code dirs) and the alias pass found no other caller: their other hits are benchmark and test sites.

remove-worktree.py acts only on a worktree that an owner record <common>/afk-worktrees/<name>.json names; for any other path remove_one returns with no output, so the WorktreeRemove/SessionEnd hook, the after-exit waiter and the SessionStart prune never touch it.
create-worktree writes the owner record only in --name mode; a branch-mode worktree (--branch/--dir) carries none, so no plugin remover (hook, waiter, prune) will ever remove it.

Inferred: /afk:bug fixer worktrees ('a fix branch off the base') are made in branch mode, so they get no owner record and are left to the skill's own S9 removal, which names no command and therefore runs through the guard as an agent command.

Uncommitted work keeps, never refuses: a tracked change, an untracked file outside RUNTIME_PATHS, a copied file changed since the copy, or an ignored file not recorded unchanged outside DISPOSABLE_DIRS/DISPOSABLE_ROOTS makes assess return a reason; without --force, remove() calls keep(), which adds {reason, shown:false} to <common>/afk-session/kept.json, prints the kept reason, a resume command and a --force remove command to stderr, and exits 0.

Unpushed commits keep the worktree the same way (kept.json + stderr commands): assess counts commits on the checked-out branch that no other local branch and no remote-tracking ref holds; a commit another branch or a remote ref holds is not unpushed.

On removal the recorded branch is deleted with `git branch -D` only when it exists and own_commits is 0, which counts against local branches only; a branch whose commits sit only on remote-tracking refs survives a removal, and --force does not delete a branch with commits of its own.

Another live session keeps, never refuses, and is reported only on stderr: on --path (hook and waiter) other_owner reads the owner record's owners list; another owner alive, unknown, or without pid/ctime makes remove_one print one 'kept worktree <path>: <reason>.' line and return, with no kept.json entry and no resume/remove commands.
The SessionStart prune skips silently (no stderr, no kept.json) every record whose owners are not all provably dead or whose move is in flight; a record naming no owner is never pruned.

No remover reads or deletes the guard's occupancy records <common>/afk-occupancy/*.json: only occupancy.py builds that path, and occupancy.claim rewrites the file with live occupants but never deletes it, so a record survives its worktree's removal.

Inferred: the remover's 'another session' test sees only sessions in the owner record (the creator, plus a session a prune adopted); a session that only mutates in the worktree is in the occupancy record, which the remover never reads, so it is not counted as busy.
A move in flight (a *.move marker under <common>/afk-session naming the path, under 600 s old) makes remove_one return with no output and the prune skip, unless --force.

A session that stands inside its worktree is not removed inline: without --force remove() prints that it is removed when the session exits and starts a detached --after-exit waiter; with --force it exits 1 telling the caller to run from outside.

The after-exit waiter polls up to 24 h, then removes via remove_one(target, False) only when the followed pid is dead and every record for the path is all_dead; otherwise it leaves the worktree to the next prune; a dirty one it keeps and records in kept.json.

--force skips three checks: the move-in-flight test, the other-owner test, and the assess verdict; it still needs an owner record, still exits 1 from inside the folder, and still keeps a branch with commits of its own. Neither hook handler passes --force.

Every plugin removal runs `git worktree remove --force` after its own assess; a git failure prints 'could not remove' and drops nothing; success drops the branch (when no own commits), the owner record and its .log, and the pane move markers.

An unknown state keeps or stops: a git failure or timeout inside assess becomes 'its state is unknown' and is kept with a kept.json entry; an Unknown before the records are read (common_dir past the hook deadline) prints 'worktree cleanup stopped and removed nothing' and records nothing; any other exception prints 'worktree cleanup skipped'; all exit 0.

remove-worktree.py exit codes: 0 for every handled outcome, 2 for a malformed call, 1 for a forced removal from inside the folder; the docstring's 'exit 1' for a malformed call is wrong (main returns 2), and no test pins the 2.

Both hook handlers exit 0 always and run under run-hook --soft, which returns 0 on a handler timeout or failure; Claude registers worktree-remove.sh for WorktreeRemove and SessionEnd (deadline 114 s), Codex only for SessionEnd (deadline 2 s, timeout 3 s), and both run worktree-prune.sh at SessionStart (deadline 57 s).

kept.json is written only by keep() and read by report_kept at SessionStart, which prints the unshown entries once as hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext (plus systemMessage when the provider declares it), marks them shown, drops entries whose folder is gone, and deletes the file when empty.

The prune also tidies leftovers: a record whose folder is gone is dropped with `git worktree prune`; a folder git no longer lists is removed only when empty, else left silently; a prune run from inside a recorded worktree adopts it.

/afk:gc keeps rather than refuses: gc-check.sh reports WORKTREE_VERDICT dirty when `git status --porcelain` is non-empty (ignored files not considered) and unmerged(n) when HEAD has commits not on the integration base, always with exit 0; the skill then skips retirement and leaves the worktree untouched, and on safe runs `git worktree remove` without --force and `git branch -d`.
/afk:gc checks no owner record, no occupancy record and no other live session; it reaches only the worktree checked out on the feature branch, whether plugin-made or not.

The PreToolUse guard is the only removal path that refuses: an agent's `git worktree remove <path>` is denied when the target is the main checkout or on a protected branch, when another live (or unknown-state) session occupies it per the occupancy record, or when git status shows tracked or untracked changes; any option (force) is denied unless ignored files remain; a git failure is a refusal naming the fault. Unpushed commits are not checked.

The guard denies every `git branch -D` / `--delete --force` and any branch delete carrying an option other than -d/--delete; `git branch -d` passes unless the branch is protected, leaving merged-state checks to git.

Inferred: remove-worktree.py's own `git worktree remove --force` and `git branch -D` run as subprocesses with AFK_WORKTREE_OP=1, not as agent tool calls, so the PreToolUse guard never judges them; the guard's -D and --force refusals bind only commands an agent types.

No test pins the guard's occupancy refusal of `git worktree remove`: the guard removal tests cover clean, dirty, protected, force-with-ignored-files and locked targets only, so that branch is unguarded.

The design-draft claim 'the existing remover refuses a changed or busy worktree' is refuted in its verb: remove-worktree.py never refuses; it keeps. A changed or unpushed worktree is kept, recorded in kept.json and the resume/remove commands are printed; a busy one is kept with one stderr line and no record; a busy one at prune is skipped with no output. Only the PreToolUse guard refuses, and only an agent's own `git worktree remove` of a changed or occupied worktree.
